page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon core across two execution threads. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. The hardware exposes advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. It is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration excludes discrete GPUs and provisioned local storage, requiring attached network storage for disk operations.

Benchmark results reflect the entry-level parallel execution capacity of the single physical core. In CPU workloads, the system records a stress-ng single-core score of 1362.9 and a multi-core score of 1806.8, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 1379.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2129.47. Uncached memory throughput measures 13.47 GB/sec for read operations and 11.35 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the instance delivers 1.61 million Redis SET operations per second, 2.41 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and generates 30.11 text tokens per second on a lightweight 135M parameter language model.

By delivering dedicated compute allocation rather than shared-core scheduling, the instance avoids noisy-neighbor throttling while maintaining lower baseline infrastructure overhead. The absence of bundled NVMe storage and GPUs prioritizes general application compute over accelerated or storage-dense tasks. This profile fits steady-state development environments, microservices, small API backends, and low-traffic web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose cloud instance provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs from 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. It includes 33 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 vector support, and 8.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration. The server includes no GPUs, bundled local storage, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external disk volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark testing reflects its entry-level multi-core footprint, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 1379.0, PassMark CPU score of 2129.47, and Redis throughput of 1.61 million SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth yields 13.47 GB/sec for uncached read operations. While constrained for high-throughput parallel compute, its dedicated execution provides stable baseline predictability, making it suitable for lightweight microservices, small web servers, background task runners, and staging environments.
